label: J-holomorphic Curves
notes: This chapter runs from printed page 17 to page 38 and turns a pointwise linear-algebra condition on the differential of a map into a nonlinear elliptic equation. Everything later in the book, from moduli spaces to Gromov-Witten theory, rests on the local structure established here before transversality or compactness appears.

label: The dbar_J Operator
notes: The nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann operator measures how far a map is from being J-holomorphic. It compares the differential with its own conjugate twisted by J on the target and j on the domain, returning a one-form valued section that vanishes exactly when the map is a pseudoholomorphic curve.

label: Complex-Linear and Antilinear Split
notes: Every real-linear differential splits canonically into a complex-linear part and a complex-antilinear part with respect to j and J. The complex-linear piece is what a holomorphic map keeps; the antilinear piece is precisely dbar_J. A curve is J-holomorphic exactly when that antilinear obstruction is zero.

label: Local Coordinate Form
notes: In a holomorphic chart on the domain the equation becomes du_s plus J of u acting on du_t equals zero. With the standard structure this is the ordinary Cauchy-Riemann system, so J-holomorphic curves are an honest nonlinear deformation of classical holomorphic maps, controlled by how J varies over the target.

label: Energy of a Curve
notes: The energy is half the integral of the squared norm of the differential measured in the metric that J and a compatible omega define. It is a conformally invariant Dirichlet-type functional, finite on compact domains, and it is the quantity whose boundedness later forces Gromov compactness of sequences of curves.

label: Energy Equals Symplectic Area
notes: For a compatible structure the energy of a J-holomorphic curve equals the integral of the pulled-back symplectic form, its omega-area. Because that area depends only on the homology class of the curve, energy is bounded a priori by topology alone, a fact with no analogue for general harmonic maps.

label: Harmonic and Conformal Maps
notes: J-holomorphic curves are conformal harmonic maps for the induced metric, so they are area-minimizing in their homology class. This links pseudoholomorphic curve theory to the classical calculus of minimal surfaces while the symplectic area identity supplies the energy bound that the harmonic-map viewpoint lacks.

label: Unique Continuation
notes: Because dbar_J is a first-order elliptic operator with a Carleman estimate, a J-holomorphic curve that vanishes to infinite order at a point, or two curves agreeing to infinite order, must coincide on the whole connected domain. This identity theorem mirrors the rigidity of ordinary holomorphic functions.

label: Critical Points and Zeros
notes: The differential of a non-constant J-holomorphic curve has only isolated zeros, and near each the map looks like a complex polynomial branch z to the m. Critical points are therefore finite in number on a compact domain, and away from them the curve is a local immersion onto its image.

label: Simple Curves and Multiple Covers
notes: A curve is somewhere injective, or simple, when some point has a single preimage and an injective differential. The set of non-injective points is then countable. Every curve is either simple or factors as a branched multiple cover of a simple curve composed with a holomorphic branched covering of the domain.

label: Local Structure of Solutions
notes: Combining the antilinear splitting, the Carleman estimate, and the branch model gives the local normal form for solutions: isolated critical points, somewhere injectivity for simple curves, and controlled intersections. In real dimension four positivity of intersections then converts this local data into the global adjunction inequality.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We defined dbar_J, identified it as the antilinear obstruction, proved energy equals symplectic area, and read off unique continuation, isolated critical points, and the simple-versus-covered dichotomy. These local facts are the foundation on which Chapter 3 builds transversality and moduli spaces of J-holomorphic curves.
